html:
The official ideology of North Korea and its ruling Workers' Party. The word means roughly self reliance, or being the master of oneself.

It is credited to Kim Il Sung, who first used the term in a speech in 1955. At the time he was purging rivals linked to Moscow and Beijing, and wanted a doctrine of his own. Juche says that the Korean revolution must be made by Koreans, in their own way, with independence in politics, self sufficiency in the economy and self defence in war. In practice it came to mean devotion to the leader, who alone can guide the masses.

In 1972 the constitution named Juche as the state's guiding idea, next to Marxism Leninism, which was later dropped. Under Kim Jong Il it was joined by the military first policy. The goal of self reliance has never matched reality: North Korea long depended on Soviet and Chinese aid, and when Soviet aid ended its economy collapsed into the famine of the 1990s.
sum: The official ideology of North Korea and its ruling Workers' Party. The word means roughly self reliance, or being the master of oneself.
